## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

'ci' : 'install', '--no-audit', '--no-fund'], { cwd: root }) mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true }) const installedHash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex') writeFileSync(stamp, installedHash) } await child(process.execPath, [join(root, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './'], { cwd: root }) root = join(root, 'dist') } if (!existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) throw new Error('Static deployment output must contain index.html.') if (process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR) writeFileSync(join(process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR, 'deployment-output.json'), JSON.stringify({ project: projectRoot, directory: resolve(root) })) const mime = { '.html':'text/html', '.js':'application/javascript', '.css':'text/css', '.json':'application/json', '.svg':'image/svg+xml', '.png':'image/png', '.jpg':'image/jpeg', '.webp':'image/webp', '.wasm':'application/wasm', '.glb':'model/gltf-binary' } const clients = new Set() const stopWatching = watchProject(root, () => { for (const client of clients) client.write('event: change\ndata: changed\n\n') }) const keepAlive = setInterval(() => { for (const client of clients) client.write(': keepalive\n\n') }, 20000) const buildWatcher = type === 'vite' ? spawn(process.execPath, [join(projectRoot, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './', '--watch'], { cwd: projectRoot, stdio: 'inherit' }) : null const server = createServer((req, res) => { try { const url = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost') if (url.pathname === '/__omgithub/live') { res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', 'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no', Connection: 'keep-alive' }) res.write(': connected\n\n') clients.add(res) req.on('close', () => clients.delete(res)) return } const path = resolve(root, '.' + decodeURIComponent(url.pathname)) if (path !== resolve(root) && !path.startsWith(resolve(root) + '/')) { res.writeHead(404); res.end(); return } const file = statSync(path).isDirectory() ? join(path, 'index.html') : path res.setHeader('Content-Type', mime[extname(file)] || 'application/octet-stream') res.setHeader('Cache-Control', url.searchParams.has('omgithub_live') ? 'no-store' : 'no-cache') const content = readFileSync(file) if (extname(file) === '.html' && url.searchParams.get('omgithub_live') === '1') { const html = content.toString() res.end(/<\/body\s*>/i.test(html) ? html.replace(/<\/body\s*>/i, `${livePreviewScript}`) : html + livePreviewScript) } else res.end(content) } catch { res.writeHead(404); res.end('Not found') } }) server.on('close', () => { stopWatching(); clearInterval(keepAlive); buildWatcher?.kill(); for (const client of clients) client.end() }) server.listen(Number(process.env.PORT || 3000), '0.0.0.0') return server } if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href) await start() ---README---

--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ```text .agents/skills//SKILL.md ``` ## 🔄 OpenCode Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Trigger] --> B[Prepare project] B --> C[Run build.md] C --> D[Run verify.md] D --> E{Public app works?} E -- No --> F[Run public-app-fix.md] F --> E E -- Yes --> G[Run completion-report.md] G --> H{Screenshots exist?} H -- No --> I[Run screenshot-evidence.md] I --> H H -- Yes --> J[Commit and push] J --> K[Create immutable project link] K --> L[Publish report] L --> M[Complete] ``` ## 🏗️ Architecture ```text ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ GitHub issue │ ──▶ │ GitHub Actions │ ──▶ │ OpenCode │ │ + issue text │ │ runner + labels │ │ + .agents │ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Build code Run tests Verify app │ │ │ └─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘ ▼ ┌────────────────────────┐ │ Commit store + preview │ └────────────────────────┘ ``` ## 🔐 Security and Access - 🔑 You do not need to create or store a project-specific AI API key. - 🖥️ You do not need to operate a dedicated build server. - ☁️ Execution happens in GitHub Actions. - 🔒 Temporary SSH and preview access exists only for the workflow run. - 👀 Review the generated commit before integrating it. - 🛡️ Restrict who can apply the `OpenCode` label in repositories that accept public issues. > “No servers needed” means no servers for you to provision or maintain. The workflow still uses GitHub-hosted Actions infrastructure and temporary workflow services. ## 📁 Project Structure ```text 📦 OMG ├─ .github/workflows/opencode.yml # 🤖 Main issue-to-project workflow ├─ wiki/opencode.md # 📖 Workflow and session notes ├─ wiki/testing.md # 🧪 Verification guidance └─ AGENTS.md # 🧭 Repository instructions ``` ## 🧪 Local Validation Validate the workflow definition before pushing changes: ```sh actionlint .github/workflows/opencode.yml git diff --check ``` ## 🐛 Troubleshooting | Problem | What to check | |---|---| | The workflow did not start | Confirm the `OpenCode` label is applied to the issue. | | A skill was not selected | Add a matching `skill/` label. | | The app URL is missing | Check the local app verification step and runner log. | | The PR was not created | Confirm OpenCode produced a diff and the workflow reached the PR step. | | The workflow ran unexpectedly | Tighten the trigger condition and trusted-user policy. | ## 🤝 Contributing Ideas, skills, game templates, verification improvements, and workflow fixes are welcome. 1. Open an issue describing the improvement. 2. Add the `OpenCode` label when you want the workflow to prototype it. 3. Review the generated commit and Open Project page carefully. 4. Add tests and runtime proof for workflow changes. ## ⭐ The Pitch The old workflow was: idea → tickets → scaffolding → setup → implementation → debugging → deployment. The OMG workflow is: **idea → issue → playable project.** If you believe software should start with a sentence instead of a sprint plan, [⭐ star the repository](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub) and try it.

- phase main.
- log.
- If hand empty => phase main.

`playCard(state, side, uid)`:
- require phase main, active side (or allow during AI main).
- cost ≤ energy.active, battle.length<5, card in hand.
- energy.active -= cost.
- remove from hand; instantiate as battle card with rested=false, summoningSick=true, enteredTurn=state.turn.
- Resolve onPlay effects:
  - draw n (from deck; if empty => lose? Real if deck out due to draw, lose. Implement `drawCards` with game over check).
  - buffSelf: card.powerBonus += n.
  - buffAll: all friendly battle including new? If effect after entry, include all. Note new card should get buff too if "all". Fine.
  - addLife: put top deck card into life (if deck nonempty, max? no max). This increases survivability.
  - koWeakest: find enemy battle card with power≤threshold, highest power or lowest? "KO an opponent's Battle Card with 15000 power or less." Choose highest power. KO it. Might trigger onKO.
  - conditional buff if life ≤3.
- Check deckout? not for play.
- Log events.
- Return events.

`onKO` triggers if card has effects (e.g., draw). Only when KO'd by opponent? Could trigger any. Implement.

Leader awakening: `checkAwaken(state, side)` if life.length <=3 and !awakened:
- set awakened=true, leader power becomes awakenPower? Base leader power field updates to `leader.awakenPower` maybe keep `power` and `basePower`; set `awakened=true`, `power = awakenPower`.
- apply awaken effect.
- log "Goku awakens!"
- event.
- Note if life gained above 3, still awakened permanently.

Damage:
`dealDamageToLeader(state, side, amount)`:

We'll just allow life cards to hand beyond limit? Better respect hand limit: if hand >=10, card goes to drop; but losing life still. Implement addToHand with limit -> drop. Yet losing life is not beneficial if hand full, but okay.

- After damage, if life.length===0 -> game over (even after adding? if 0).

Potential rule: if leader has 0 life before attack, next damage wins. Good.

`resolveAttack`:
input declared attack object:
```
{
 attackerSide, attackerUid (or 'leader'),

}
```
Controller selects combos before resolve. Combo cards are removed from hand when selected? To avoid UI complexity, `commitCombo(state, side, uids)` discards them and returns bonus, but if cancellation needed... We can handle at resolve: validate still in hand, remove them. UI selection doesn't mutate until confirm. Good.
- Compute attacker base: if leader -> leader.power (with awaken), if card -> power+bonus. Use helper `currentPower`.
- Target base: if blocker -> blocker power; else leader or card.
- Add combo values: sum card.combo for selected uids + maybe buffs? Combos are flat.
- If target is leader and attack > defense: damage = 1 + (attacker doubleStrike ? 1:0). Apply.
- If target is battle card/blocker and attack > defense: KO target.
- Attacker rests: if battle card, rested=true, attacked=true. If leader, leader.attacked=true.
- Always rest attacker.
- Remove combo cards from hands to drop.
- Log details.
- Events: attack, combo, damage, ko, awaken, win.
- Check gameover.
- `state.phase` remains main.
- If attacker was leader and attacked, can't attack again.
- Target battle cards must be rested; validate.

`declareAttack(state, side, attackerUid, targetUid)` returns info:
- validate attacker active (not rested), not summoning sick, not attacked; leader only once.
- valid targets: enemy leader, enemy rested battle cards.
- target has no protection keywords? no.
- returns `{ok, attackInfo}` with base values and possible blockers:
   - blockers: enemy battle cards with blocker keyword, active, not summoningSick irrelevant, not the target.
- UI uses `attackInfo.blockers`.
- Blockers can block for leader or for battle card (including if target is a rested battle card? If attacking a rested battle card, can a blocker redirect? In DBFW, Blocker can redirect attacks to itself including against cards. We'll allow).
- `applyBlocker(state, info, blockerUid)`:
   - validate blocker belongs to defender, active, blocker keyword; set info.blockerUid and rest blocker? Rest should happen at resolution or immediately. Do immediately? If attack canceled, blocker rests for nothing. We'll rest on resolution. But if combo UI uses target, info target changed; okay.
- `resolveAttack(state, info, attackComboUids, defenseComboUids)`.
- Ensure combos belong to correct sides/hands.

`validAttackTargets(state, side, attackerUid)`.

AI attack selection needs enumerate options without mutations. Implement `getAttackOptions(state, side)` returns array of {attackerUid,targetUid,attackerPower,targetPower, isLethal? etc.}. But blockers complicate. AI can send attack and handle blocker.
- Use engine functions.

### AI implementation detail

We'll implement AI as state-driven controller in ui.js to allow async delays and player prompts. ai.js exports pure decision functions:

- `chooseMulligan(state, side)`: returns uids.
- `chooseCharge(state, side)`: uid.
- `choosePlay(state, side)`: uid or null.
- `chooseAttack(state, side)`: {attackerUid,targetUid} or null.
- `chooseAttackCombo(state, attackInfo)`: uids.
- `chooseDefenseCombo(state, attackInfo)`: uids.
- `chooseBlocker(state, attackInfo, side)`: uid|null.

AI difficulty parameter from stage (1-6). Use `level`:
- combo caution: chance to make mistakes? Deterministic with RNG maybe. Use randomness for low levels: e.g., 20% skip good play, 25% not charge optimal. But avoid frustrating. Difficulty also deck strength.
- Implement thresholds:
  - attack combo efficiency: level>=2.
  - defense combo: level>=1; use to save life if within 2 cards; level 1 may fail sometimes.
  - blocker: level>=2.
  - choosePlay: level 1 random among top 3; level 6 best.
  - chooseAttack: level 1 may attack only obvious; higher considers combos and lethal.
We'll make AI competent but not perfect.

`chooseCharge` scoring:
- Keep cards with low cost and high combo? Charging removes from hand permanently, so charge worst card: no on-play value, low combo, high cost. Compute playValue = power/5000 + combo/4000 + keywords bonus + onPlay. If energy low early, keep cheap playables. Score card desirability; charge lowest. If hand has 5+ and worst low, fine.
- Avoid charging a card if it's the only playable next turn? Could keep 1 cheap. Simpler: charge lowest.
- For high level, ensure curve: don't charge cost≤1 if no other; but no biggie.

`choosePlay`:
- Evaluate all affordable cards. Score:
  - base power/1000 + combo/2000 + keywords (rush 2.5, blocker 1.5 or more if life low) + onPlay draw 2 + buff all 2.
  - Cost efficiency: score - cost*0.2 maybe.
  - If board full return null.
  - If energy remaining high and can play more, loop.
  - Low level: choose randomly among top 2.
  - If life ≤2, prioritize blockers.
  - Avoid playing a card that has no value? All okay.
- Keep energy for leader? no.
- Play until none.

`chooseAttack`:
- Get own attackers: leader if !attacked; battle cards active !rested !summoningSick.
- Enemy leader power, enemy rested battle cards.
- For each attacker, target leader:
  - base = attacker power; available combo total from hand (choose cheapest/lowest value combos? AI can use any; select cards with lowest "keep value" first). `maxCombo = sum of top combo cards maybe`.
  - canDamageWithCombo = base + maxCombo > leaderPower; if base > leaderPower, damage likely.
  - value = 10 + damage*20 if base > leaderPower; if need combo, value = 8 + damage*15 - combosUsed*2.
  - If enemy life==1 and potential damage ≥1, huge.
  - But defender may have blockers. Compute effective: if enemy has active blocker with high power, attack may get blocked. Value reduced unless attack can beat blocker too. Also attacking forces blocker to rest, which is value.
- Battle card targets: only rested cards. If base > target power: value = 5 + target cost*2 + target power/10000*2; if target has high power/threat. If need combo, maybe value less; AI shouldn't spend combos to KO small cards unless it denies big threat.
- Pick highest value > 0. Avoid attacking with blockers unless value high or lethal; penalty 3.
- If no attack, end.
- Target choice ordering: choose most valuable.
- For AI attacking player leader, player may block; fine.
- For AI attack combos: after blocker resolution:
  - Need combo to beat target power; if target is battle card, only spend combos if total combo value needed and target value worth it, and not overkill. Choose combo cards with lowest keep priority, perhaps up to needed + small buffer. Defense will react, but AI doesn't know; at higher levels, overcommit? Could add a buffer against expected defense combos. Simpler: spend minimum needed, capped by cards.
  - For leader target, if base + available > defense, maybe spend to deal damage; but defender can combo too, so overcommit is risky. Use enough to beat current defense + 5000 buffer at high level. If damage would be lethal, commit everything.
  - If base already > defense, no combos.
  - Battle card target: if base > target, no combos. If not, only use combos if can KO and target high value, and total combo cost ≤2 cards.
- For AI defense combos:
  - If target is leader and life > 1, spend combos only if close to survive and would lose life otherwise; use minimum to push defense ≥ attack (strictly greater? need defense >= attack to prevent damage? Rule is attacker > defender to damage, so defense >= attack prevents). Use minimal cards; at high level, consider saving cards for next turn if damage not lethal. At life 1, commit all. At low level, maybe only block if easy.
  - If target battle card, maybe combo to save high-value card if close and card cost high. Otherwise no.
- Blocker AI:
  - If can block to prevent life loss and blocker survives or trades favorably, do so. Evaluate each active blocker: if attack power > blocker power, blocker dies; value if saves life. If life 1, always block with any. Else block if blocker power + possible combos? AI could combo the blocker. Keep simple: block if blocker power >= attack power (survives) OR saves lethal OR blocker is low value versus damage. At high level, also block if blocker dies but saves life and blocker cost < 3. At low level, block 50% maybe.
  - However the attack power before attacker combos; attacker might combo after blocker. AI doesn't know. Blocking based on current attack power may be punished. It's okay.
  - If target already battle card, blocking to save it with a stronger blocker could be good; but usually not.
- Note AI as defender has active blockers; player attack UI prompts player? For player attack, controller automatically decides AI blocker and combos, then does player attacker combos before? Actual order: attacker combos, then defender combos. Blocker decision happens before combos. So controller: player declares -> AI may block -> player combo -> AI defense combo -> resolve. Good.
- For AI attack: AI declares -> player may block (prompt) -> AI attack combo (recompute) -> player defense combo (prompt) -> resolve.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable single-player card game inspired by Dragon Ball Fusion World in the existing PlayGround repo.
- Continue from the previous failed run (no code had been written) and finish the game now.

## Requirements
- Card game based on Dragon Ball Fusion World.
- Single-player only.
- Complete and playable; do not ask clarifying questions.
- Prefer browser game; must run via static `index.html` because runtime serves static files unless a Vite project exists.
- Mobile support expected: responsive layout and touch controls.
- Note reasonable assumptions briefly when finished.

## Decisions
- Build an original fan-made game titled **Dragon Ball: Fusion World**, with all visuals generated procedurally as SVG/CSS and all audio synthesized with WebAudio; no external copyrighted assets.
- Static browser game with plain script tags (no build step), files under `js/`.
- Fixed 50-card decks per leader; no deckbuilding.
- Campaign of 6 stages: Desert Duel (Yamcha), Frieza Force, Android Invasion, Cell Games, Majin Awakening, God of Destruction (Beerus).
- Playable leaders: Goku (awaken draw 1), Vegeta (awaken buff all +5000), Piccolo (awaken add life), Frieza (unlock after clearing stage 3; awaken KO ≤15000).
- Rules implemented: leader/life/energy, charge phase, battle area max 5, combo cards, Blockers, Rush, Double Strike, awakening at ≤3 life, deck-out loss, hand limit 10, energy cap 10.
- Save progress in `localStorage` under `dbfw_save_v2`; stars based on remaining life; unlock next stage and Frieza after stage 3.
- Use original data/engine/AI architecture with deterministic RNG and Node simulation tests.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected repo and confirmed prior run failed with no implementation.
- Created `js/data.js`: factions, keywords, 45+ cards, 10 leaders, 10 validated 50-card decks, 6 stages, helpers and validation.
- Created `js/engine.js`: full rules engine (setup, mulligan, turns, charge, play, combat, blockers, combos, damage, awakening, KO, deck-out, logs, stats).
- Created `js/ai.js`: charge/play/attack/blocker/combo and mulligan heuristics scaled by level 1–6.
- Created `tests/sim.cjs`: headless simulation harness; **288/288 simulations completed cleanly** across all stages/leaders/seeds.
- Created `js/art.js`: procedural SVG character portraits and technique art for all cards/leaders.
- Created `js/audio.js`: synthesized SFX for clicks, draw, play, charge, attack, hit, block, KO, damage, combo, awaken, win/lose.
- Created `index.html` with script/style wiring and metadata.
- Created `styles.css`: full visual system, card frames, menu, board, hand fan, modals, combo/blocker panels, responsive/mobile rules, animations, FX.
- Started `js/ui.js` but the write failed because the payload exceeded output limits; no usable UI file was saved.

### Active
- Implement `js/ui.js` from scratch, split into multiple smaller writes/edits to avoid output limits.
- UI must cover: title screen, leader/stage select, deck viewer, how-to-play, settings, VS intro, mulligan, battle board rendering, hand/attack/combos/blockers, AI turn orchestration, log, result screen, save progression, toasts, attack FX, keyboard controls, debug API, query-screen support.
- Then run browser verification and iterate on visuals/gameplay.

### Blocked
- No code blockers. Only the single large `write` to `js/ui.js` failed; use several smaller tool calls instead.

## Next Move
1. Create `js/ui.js` in multiple chunks (helpers/save/background/menu; battle render; interactions/AI; modals/result/FX/init), or create a minimal skeleton then append with `edit`.
2. Ensure `index.html` loads scripts in order: `data.js`, `engine.js`, `ai.js`, `art.js`, `audio.js`, `ui.js`.
3. Run `node tests/sim.cjs` again and add focused engine tests if needed.
4. Start static server on port 3002 (`PORT=3002 node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs"`) and verify with Playwright.
5. Screenshot title, stage select, battle, mulligan, combo, and mobile layout; fix overflow/visual defects.
6. Exercise a full battle via Playwright/click-through, verify win/lose/result/save progression.
7. Commit changes.

## Relevant Files
- `js/ui.js`: missing; main remaining deliverable.
- `js/engine.js`: complete game rules API used by UI.
- `js/data.js`: cards/leaders/decks/stages.
- `js/ai.js`: AI decision functions used by UI and tests.
- `js/art.js`: `ART.art(key,{faction,label})` returns SVG strings.
- `js/audio.js`: `AUDIO.play(name)`, `setEnabled`, `resume`, `ensure`.
- `styles.css`: all classes for UI; check names before writing UI.
- `index.html`: static entry, script order.
- `tests/sim.cjs`: headless simulation, currently 288/288 clean.
- `.omgithub/conversation.json`: prior context, no implementation.

## Important Context
- Working directory: `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround`; branch `opencode/41947073666`; working tree changes are currently uncommitted.
- Runtime static server: `PORT=3002 node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs"`; no `package.json` should be added (unsupported by runtime unless Vite).
- Playwright available at `playwright-cli`; headless Chromium also available via `/home/runner/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/node_modules/playwright`.
- UI must be plain browser scripts, not ES modules; `.mjs` is served with wrong MIME.
- Engine API: `createBattle`, `mulligan`, `startTurn`, `chargeCard`, `skipCharge`, `playCard`, `getAttackers`, `getValidTargets`, `getBlockers`, `declareAttack`, `setBlocker`, `resolveAttack`, `endTurn`, `forfeit`, `effectivePower`, `fmt`.
- `declareAttack` returns `{ok, info, blockers}`; `info` has `attackerPower`, `targetPower`, `doubleStrike`, `blockerUid`, `targetSide`.
- `resolveAttack(state, info, attackComboUids, defenseComboUids)` returns `{ok, events, attackPower, targetPower, hit}`.
- Every deck recipe validated at 50 cards; `D.validate()` returns `[]`.
- No commit has been made yet.
